title: Offline change-window and manifest-verification acceptance for VPC private deploys
creator: Asha Patel
body:
Summary:
This ticket captures the requirements and acceptance criteria for a deterministic, timeboxed offline change window and artifact-manifest verification process for Private/VPC deployments. The goal is to give operator teams a repeatable, low-risk playbook to apply upgrades or configuration changes in sites with limited or no egress, constrained bandwidth, and strict air-gapped policies.

Background and motivation:
Many customers operate air-gapped or heavily restricted VPCs where upgrades must be performed with bounded outbound connectivity and within a scheduled maintenance window. Past incidents show two recurring failure modes: (1) partial artifact syncs that leave heterogeneous control-plane/agent versions, and (2) silent corruption or mismatch of manifests leading to node drift. We need an operable acceptance contract for any Private deploy upgrade flow that covers bandwidth-capped initial syncs, deterministic manifest verification, and clear rollback boundaries.

Scope (in-scope):
- Define the offline change-window contract: maximum allowed wall-clock duration, per-cluster bandwidth cap targets, and percent-of-nodes allowed to be out-of-sync during a window.
- Specify manifest schema and signed-hash verification requirements for all operator-installable artifacts (images, manifests, metadata tarballs).
- Define a staged delta-only sync mode to minimize transfer volume and predictable time estimates.
- Provide operator runbook steps for preflight validation, canary node selection (node-level canary + control-plane canary), telemetry gating, and rollback initiation.
- Acceptance tests (automated harness) that emulate bandwidth throttling, interrupted transfers, corrupted manifests, and full offline rollbacks.

Out-of-scope:
- Design or implementation of new image transport protocols (we rely on existing mirror/rsync/airgap tooling).
- Changes to customer network architecture beyond documented prerequisites.

Success metrics / non-functional constraints:
- Max total transfer bytes for a full cluster upgrade should be estimable and honored within +/- 20% under the declared bandwidth cap.
- Manifest hash verification must detect any artifact mismatch 100% of the time in tests (no false negatives).
- Canary failure detection time must be under 10 minutes from the first failed healthcheck.
- Rollback completion time target: full rollback to previous control-plane snapshot within the declared window length.

Acceptance criteria (pass/fail checklist):
1) Preflight checks: a documented preflight run that verifies node disk space, time sync, and operator version compatibility must exist and succeed on a representative canary before any cluster-wide action. Steps and expected outputs recorded in runbook.
2) Manifest signing and verification: all artifacts provided for the upgrade are accompanied by a signed manifest containing sha256 hashes. The operator verifies signatures against customer-trusted keys (acceptance requires a test where signature tampering is detected and aborts the upgrade).
3) Bandwidth-capped sync: the upgrade procedure must support a bandwidth cap configuration (kbps) and demonstrate empirically via an automated test that total wall-clock time for canary + 50% nodes completes within the timebox given the cap.
4) Delta-only payloads: the sync mechanism must only transfer changed files between versions for non-canary nodes. Acceptance test verifies transferred bytes reduced by at least 60% vs full payload in a controlled scenario.
5) Canary gating and automatic stop: if canary nodes or the control-plane canary fail healthchecks or manifest verification, the system must automatically halt rollout and mark the window as failed. Acceptance test triggers a canary failure and verifies halt.
6) Deterministic rollback: a single documented command must revert cluster artifacts to the pre-upgrade snapshot. Acceptance test simulates a canary regression and executes rollback; cluster returns to functioning baseline and telemetry signals are collected.
7) Offline retry semantics: interrupted syncs must be resumable without restarting from scratch. Test must interrupt transfer at multiple points and resume successfully with no corrupted artifacts.
8) Audit trail & observability: upgrade events, manifest hashes, node-level verification results, and bandwidth metrics are recorded to logs/telemetry. Acceptance requires a dashboard panel and archived run-level artifact in S3/drive for postmortem.

Test plan and harness:
- Automated harness in the CI lab simulating an islanded VPC using iptables to drop/limit connections. Test cases: full successful window, manifest tamper abort, interrupted transfers + resume, canary regression + rollback, and bandwidth oversubscription scenario.
- Test artifacts referenced: https://confluence.redwood.ai/private-deploys/offline-window-prd (draft), GH PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/private-operator/pull/421, CI harness pipeline: https://ci.redwood.ai/job/private-offline-tests/421.

Runbook preview (operator steps):
1) Run preflight checks and export pre-upgrade snapshot and manifest (cli: rwdctl preflight --export).
2) Start canary in delta-only mode (cli: rwdctl upgrade --canary --bandwidth 500k).
3) Monitor canary health (dashboard link) for 10 minutes; if green, proceed in waves (50% nodes then 100%).
4) On any manifest verification failure, run rwdctl upgrade --abort; collect artifacts and trigger rollback.
5) After successful completion, produce signed acceptance note and archive run artifacts.

Rollout and fallback strategy:
- Default: two-wave rollout (canary 3 nodes or 10% whichever larger, then remaining nodes).
- Fallback: immediate abort and rollback if canary fails or if transfer rates exceed 120% of planned window estimate.
- Escalation: if rollback fails, move to emergency physical-media fallback (instructions included in runbook).

Telemetry and monitoring gates:
- Required telemetry: per-node artifact checksum status, transfer bytes, transfer duration, time-to-health after restart, operator error counts.
- Gates: rollout cannot proceed if any gate metric is outside expected thresholds for the canary window.

Open questions / decisions required:
- Key management: final decision on whether customers will upload a key OR the operator will verify signatures against a hardware-backed key stored in the control plane. Action: Security to advise by 2025-02-24.
- Bandwidth cap default: propose 1Mbps per cluster as default; PM to validate with Sales for customer impact.

Follow-ups & action items:
- ENG: implement resumeable delta-sync prototype and wire manifest signature verification into operator. (ENG-20011)
- Security: define key onboarding UX and threat model for signed manifests. (SEC-1045)
- DX: create a customer-facing maintenance-window checklist and runbook excerpt for the console. (DOC-88)

Notes / recent updates:
- 2025-02-12: initial draft reviewed with Solutions Eng; they requested a shorter default window and clearer canary sizing heuristics.
- 2025-02-15: added explicit delta-only payload requirement after discussions with infra about repeated full sync cost.
- 2025-02-18: Security confirmed high-level signing approach; pending detailed KMS integration design.
